items.title: Delegate – AI eng manager running team of agents for async multitasking
items.raw_excerpt: I built Delegate because I was tired of babysitting AI coding agents. Cursor is fast but you're in the chair. I wanted to hand off five tasks and come back to PRs with agents already having peer reviewed each other's code. Delegate is a browser-based tool where you talk to an AI manager. It breaks down your request into tasks, assigns AI agents, manages git (worktrees, branches, merges), and notifies you when code is ready for final approval. Post-approval, code is merged in local git repo's main. It's open source (MIT), runs locally, uses Claude under the hood (BYOK). Demo video: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d2f5a8f-8bae-45b... What works: parallel tasks, planning conversations, code review before merge, git isolation. What's rough: setup on non-trivial repos, agent quality

excerpt_i18n.zh: 2月21日，据清华大学智能产业研究院消息，清华大学智能产业研究院AIR团队于2026年2月发表在《npj Artificial Intelligence》的研究《驾驶任务中的人类与算法视觉注意力》，以自动驾驶这一安全关键领域为载体，首次通过“人类眼动追踪实验+算法对比验证”的双轨设计，系统性拆解了人类与算法视觉注意力的本质差异。其核心价值在于提出人类驾驶注意力的三阶段量化划分框架，并证实：算法视觉理解的核心缺陷是缺乏“语义显著性提取能力”，而融入人类检查阶段的语义注意力，能以经济高效的方式填补专业算法的“语义鸿沟”与大模型的“接地鸿沟”，无需依赖大规模预训练。
excerpt_i18n.en: On February 21, according to the Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR) at Tsinghua University, a study titled "Human and Algorithmic Visual Attention in Driving Tasks," published by the AIR team in the journal *npj Artificial Intelligence* in February 2026, systematically dissected the fundamental differences between human and algorithmic visual attention for the first time through a dual-track design of "human eye-tracking experiments + algorithmic comparative validation," using the safety-critical field of autonomous driving as a vehicle. Its core value lies in proposing a three-stage quantitative framework for human driving attention and demonstrating that the key deficiency in algorithmic visual understanding is the lack of "semantic salience extraction capability." Incorporating semantic attention from the human inspection stage can efficiently bridge the "semantic gap" in specialized algorithms and the "grounding gap" in large models without relying on large-scale pre-training.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 21 de febrero, según informó el Instituto de Investigación de Industria Inteligente de la Universidad de Tsinghua, el equipo del instituto publicó en febrero de 2026 en la revista "npj Artificial Intelligence" un estudio titulado "Atención visual humana y algorítmica en tareas de conducción". Utilizando el campo crítico de seguridad de la conducción autónoma como plataforma, este estudio desglosa sistemáticamente las diferencias esenciales entre la atención visual humana y la algorítmica mediante un diseño dual de "experimento de seguimiento ocular humano + verificación comparativa de algoritmos". Su valor central radica en proponer un marco de división cuantitativa en tres etapas para la atención humana en la conducción, y confirmar que el defecto principal en la comprensión visual algorítmica es la falta de capacidad para extraer la prominencia semántica.
